posts.cooked:
As a relatively newer player, I could see something like that being useful.  For example, if a group is about to have their first fight against Citizen Dawn, having done all right against Omnitron and Blade.  They're jumping up to a 3, so they want to make sure they're using some of the stronger heroes to make sure they don't get destroyed this first time.  Later they can try again with different mixes, but for that first time they want to make sure they've got a fighting chance.  So a list of who's considered good and who's considered weaker might help them, until they've gotten a better grasp on the heroes themselves and how the villains play.

It can also help players, like the OP here, who has a really awful slog of it in some fight, to find out that "Oh! Turns out I happened to be using three characters that people generally regard as being on the weaker side."  They may be more willing to try that villain again once they know that they just stumbled into a slightly rougher line-up.  They should also know about particular matchups being good or bad, of course, even if everyone agreed on some sort of raw rankings that wouldn't be the end of the discussion---but I would think the rankings can be a useful shorthand, at least for some.

posts.name: HeroComplex
posts.cooked:
I agree, I alluded to that at the end of the post.  But I think it's fair to assume that not every new player is going to have perfect information, have read the relevant guides, etc.  Some just want a quick snapshot, and since I don't know that there's a comprehensive, brief mapping of how each hero does situationally, a quick snapshot of generally how each hero tends to be regarded is useful.  If someone has or wants to create the more useful resource, I'm all for that.  It's just in the absence of it that I'm saying I could understand the value of "rankings" as a shorthand for newer players.

 

Edit: Also, just to say---I'm not a proponent of tiers/rankings or anything, my goal wasn't to jump in and push for them.  You were asking what the value was, so I thought I would chime in and offer a possible answer, that's all.  We have two players, so we tend to half-randomize our games right now---we each pick one hero from a small randomized set, and choose from the full list for each of our second heroes.  We do end up picking heroes that we tend not to use as much, which is good, but we never feel like we're stuck with a team that we won't enjoy or that we don't know how to use.  (Or that has no damage, or something.)  We wouldn't really use formal rankings for our character selections, but it's potentially helpful for us to think about whether or first two heroes tend to be powerhouses, support, etc., so that we can balance our teams a bit.  In case that helps explain a bit where my perspective is coming from.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
I would say that giving heroes a "rank" implies that some are outright better/worse than others - this isn't true. Depending on luck of the draw, a hero can have a really bad day and do nothing or they might wipe the floor with whatever's thrown at them (more/less so if the villain and/or environment has a good/bad draw themselves, of course). I think it's better to (as some people have already done in the past on this forum) try to sum up each hero with a quick sentence. Some examples...

Wraith - Good all-rounder, can dish out damage and destroy ongoing/environment cards as well as give herself a bit of healing/soak but has a bad time against equipment destruction.

Legacy - Excels at buffing other heroes' damage and can deal a bit himself but relies pretty heavily on ongoings to achieve his full potential and has no means of destroying non-target cards.

Ra - Really good at burning stuff in a variety of ways, but doesn't really do much else. Has a decent mix of ongoings and one-shots and only one equipment card.

So I didn't mention everything that each of those heroes can do (eg no mention of stuff like Trust Fund, Smoke Bombs, Danger Sense, or Excavation), but if I'm trying to briefly sum up a character for someone who's completely new to the game I don't think I'd need to go into specifics that detailed, but rather just give the briefest summary possible. And then if someone has played a couple of games and wanted a hero a bit different to the one(s) they'd just played, I could suggest someone based on what they liked about whomever they'd already used - If someone played Wraith and then decided "Hmm that was fun, but I'd prefer to do more damage via one-shots and be less reliant on equipment" I'd suggest they play Tempest, for example.

We post them to see if the way we view the heroes are different from others.  I learned a lot after thinking about, posting and then looking at others tier lists.  It brought up a lot of debateand I ended up playing a few heroes differently.  (Ra for example, I find him overrated as a damage dealer, but I've learned to use his other cards a lot better, and he's really good)

posts.name: Edwin
posts.cooked: The difference between tiers in SOTM is very small compared to most games, but it definitely exists.  Wraith is an absolute top-notch hero; that fact should be obvious to everyone.  Who else can draw a card, tutor one of a half-dozen great Equipment cards straight into play, play another card, and then use one or even two powers?  Nightmist and the Scholar can become virtually invincible if they have time to set up, Ra does unparallelled amounts of damage, Unity's army of bots is unstoppable against anything other than AOE damage (or horrific luck), Tempest is an amazing beatstick with only a few weaknesses, and Legacy boosts every team's win percentages through the roof.  While other characters may not be useless, they may have trouble comparing to these high marks (Tempest, Unity and Ra are debatable as being in that top category; Wraith and Legacy are not).  And there are a few heroes - Bunker is the one most often mentioned - who just don't tend to measure up as well.  They can certainly contribute, and they have a few specialized tools which may occasionally make them the star of a match, but very seldom do they pull more than their fair share of the weight.  Both Tachyon's Lightspeed Barrage and Bunker's Omni-Cannon are good for large amounts of damage, for example, but Bunker has to burn huge numbers of cards and possibly risk losing them to equipment destruction, while Tachyon doesn't have to do anything but play cards normally.  No hero is ever completely useless, but there are definite inequalities in exactly how useful some heroes are and how often, compared to others.  I do not believe I have ever once seen a game where Legacy's presence was not a tremendous, continual benefit; I definitely cannot say the same about Mr. Fixer or Parse.
